classification.difficultyReason: Apply fixed positions, grouping and relative-order symmetry to seven distinct letters.

content.prompt: Find how many arrangements of the letters of the word UNIFORM are possible:

children.label: a
children.prompt: if the vowels must occupy the first, middle and last positions,

answer.worked:
The vowels are U, I, O; the consonants are N, F, R, M.
Arrange the 3 vowels in the first, middle and last positions, then arrange the 4 consonants in the remaining positions.
$$3!\times4!=144$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: if the word must start with U and end with M,

answer.worked:
Fix U at the start and M at the end. Arrange the remaining 5 letters.
$$5!=120$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: if all the consonants must be in a group at the end of the word,

answer.worked:
The consonants N, F, R, M occupy the last 4 positions. Arrange the 3 vowels in the first 3 positions, then arrange the 4 consonants.
$$3!\times4!=144$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: if the M is somewhere to the right of the U.

answer.worked:
Swapping U and M pairs each arrangement having M to the right of U with one having M to the left of U. Therefore half of all arrangements satisfy the restriction.
$$\frac{7!}{2}=2520$$
